_meta.source: Fig. 3, Andriuc, Siron & Persson, Surface Science 758 (2025) 122745 (co2red_tio2.pdf)
_meta.note: Paper states 'Data will be made available on request' -- no numeric table was published. These values were extrapolated by pixel-position extraction from the published scatter plot (marker centroids calibrated against the plot's own axis gridlines, DPI-rendered from the embedded figure), not read from any released dataset.
_meta.method: Axis gridlines fit via linear regression on detected gridline pixel positions (R^2=1 by construction, 6 x-ticks / 7 y-ticks). Marker centroids found per legend color+shape via connected-component analysis; overlapping markers in the dense cluster near the origin were split via distance-transform peak-finding and confirmed by visual comparison against the legend glyphs.
_meta.uncertainty_eV: ~0.05-0.1 eV typical (axis calibration is exact; dominant error is marker-centroid localization against a JPEG-compressed, ~1300px-wide embedded image). The 'TiO2 (anatase), (111) [0.125]' row has the lowest shape-match confidence -- it sits in the most crowded cluster and was assigned by elimination after the other 9 anatase markers were matched to their legend glyphs one-by-one; its position is still precise, only the facet label carries slightly more uncertainty.
_meta.sanity_check: Residuals against the paper's own reported oxide linear fit (CO = 1.11*H + 0.66, R^2=0.77) have mean ~0.00 and std ~0.76 eV, consistent with the paper's R^2. The two largest outliers -- TiO2 rutile (111)[0.446] and TiO2 anatase (101)[0.355] -- are exactly the two surfaces the paper's own text calls out by name as having 'strongly negative adsorption energies for both CO and H', which cross-validates the extraction against the paper's prose.
